subject: physics_2
question_text: Define mean free path of electron in a conductor.

verification.note: The mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: mean free path = average distance a free electron travels between two successive collisions with the ions of the conductor; λ = v τ with v the average (thermal) speed and τ the relaxation time; order of magnitude in copper about 10⁻⁸ m.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Inside a conductor, a free electron keeps
colliding with the ions of the metal.
The average distance a free electron travels
between two successive collisions is called
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words average and successive collisions are both part of the definition.
steps.why: A single electron travels a different distance before each collision, so only the average over very many collisions is a fixed, usable number for the material.
common_mistakes: Writing distance travelled per second — that is a speed, not a path length.
Leaving out average, which makes the quantity undefined.

recall.must_convey: That the mean free path is the average distance a free electron travels between two successive collisions in the conductor.
accept: average distance between two successive collisions

steps.memory_tip: Three words carry the mark: average, between, collisions.

steps.label: The relation λ = v τ
lines: If v is the average speed of the electron and
τ is the average time between two successive
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name both symbols: v is the average speed, τ is the relaxation time.
steps.why: Distance is speed multiplied by time. The average distance between collisions must therefore be the average speed multiplied by the average time between collisions.
common_mistakes: Using the drift velocity for v. The electron moves at its thermal speed between collisions; drift velocity is far smaller.
Calling τ the time period. It is the average time between collisions, called the relaxation time.

recall.must_convey: That the mean free path lambda equals the average speed v times the relaxation time tau.
accept: speed multiplied by time between collisions
reject: average distance between two successive collisions

steps.memory_tip: Distance = speed × time, so λ = v τ with τ the time between collisions.

insider_note: The definition mark needs the exact words average distance between two successive collisions — a vague between collisions sentence loses it.
